stem: The largest and best-known prehistoric rock painting site in India is located at __________.
solution: The Bhimbetka caves in Madhya Pradesh have the richest and best-known prehistoric rock paintings in India.

stem: The Bhimbetka rock shelters are located in the state of __________.
solution: Bhimbetka is situated in the Raisen district of Madhya Pradesh, in the Vindhya hills.

stem: Bhimbetka has been recognised by UNESCO as a __________.
solution: The Rock Shelters of Bhimbetka are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

stem: The prehistoric rock paintings are broadly classified according to the periods: Upper Palaeolithic, Mesolithic and __________.
solution: The paintings span the Upper Palaeolithic, Mesolithic and Chalcolithic periods.

stem: The largest number of rock paintings at Bhimbetka belong to the __________ period.
solution: The Mesolithic period has the largest number of paintings, rich in themes and colours.

stem: The most common colours used in prehistoric rock paintings were __________.
options: various shades of white, red and green
solution: The paintings mainly use natural colours — white, red (from haematite/geru) and green.

stem: The red colour used in prehistoric paintings was obtained from __________.
solution: Red was derived from haematite (known as geru in India).

stem: The green colour in prehistoric rock paintings was obtained from a green variety of a stone called __________.
solution: Green came from a green variety of a chalcedony (a form of quartz).

stem: The subjects most commonly depicted in Upper Palaeolithic rock paintings were __________.
options: large animals like bison, elephants and rhinos
solution: Upper Palaeolithic paintings show large animal figures such as bisons, tigers, elephants and rhinos.

stem: Mesolithic rock paintings are characterised by the depiction of __________.
options: hunting scenes and smaller, more numerous figures
solution: Mesolithic paintings show lively hunting scenes with smaller, more numerous human and animal figures.

stem: The prehistoric rock paintings at Lakhudiyar are located in the state of __________.
solution: Lakhudiyar, on the banks of the River Suyal, is in Uttarakhand.

stem: At Lakhudiyar, the paintings are done in three colours: white, black and __________.
solution: Lakhudiyar paintings use white, black and red ochre.

stem: The wavy lines, rectangle-filled geometric designs and groups of dots at Lakhudiyar are examples of __________ in prehistoric art.
options: hand-linked dancing human figures and patterns
solution: Lakhudiyar shows humans, animals and geometric patterns including hand-linked dancing figures.

stem: Prehistoric people made paintings mainly on the walls and ceilings of __________.
solution: Early humans painted on the walls and ceilings of natural rock shelters and caves.

stem: The prehistoric rock shelters of Kupgallu, Piklihal and Tekkalkota are located in __________.
solution: These rock painting sites are in South India (the Karnataka–Andhra region).

stem: The paintings that superimpose newer figures over older ones show that the caves were __________.
options: used and painted over many periods
solution: Superimposition of paintings indicates repeated use of the same surfaces over many periods.

stem: One of the most striking scenes at Bhimbetka is a large __________ surrounded by hunters.
solution: A famous Bhimbetka scene depicts a large animal (a boar/bison) surrounded by tiny human hunters.

stem: The brushes used by prehistoric painters were most likely made from __________.
solution: Prehistoric painters likely used brushes of plant fibre or hair.

stem: The scientific study of prehistoric paintings tells us mainly about the __________ of early humans.
options: daily life, hunting and social activities
solution: The paintings reveal the hunting, food, and social life of prehistoric humans.

stem: The prehistoric caves of Jogimara, with paintings, are located in __________.
solution: The Jogimara caves with early paintings are in the Amarnath area of Chhattisgarh.

stem: Which of the following was NOT a colour commonly used by prehistoric rock painters?
solution: Bright blue was not available; the palette was mainly white, red and green from natural minerals.

stem: The pigments used for prehistoric paintings were ground and mixed with __________ to make them stick.
options: a binding medium such as animal fat or gum
solution: Natural pigments were mixed with a binder like animal fat or plant gum.

stem: The white pigment used in prehistoric paintings was often obtained from __________.
solution: White was obtained from limestone or lime-based materials.

stem: The Bhimbetka caves were discovered by the archaeologist __________.
solution: V. S. Wakankar discovered the Bhimbetka rock shelters in 1957–58.

stem: The theme of dance in a group of joined human figures is most typical of the __________ period paintings.
solution: Group dancing and community scenes are characteristic of the Mesolithic paintings.

stem: Chalcolithic paintings at Bhimbetka show evidence of __________ between cave dwellers and settled agricultural communities.
solution: Chalcolithic paintings reveal contact and exchange between the cave people and settled farming communities.

stem: The animals shown in prehistoric paintings are often depicted with great __________.
solution: Prehistoric artists depicted animals with remarkable accuracy and vitality.

stem: Prehistoric rock art in India is important because it represents the __________ of Indian art.
solution: Rock paintings mark the earliest beginnings of art in the Indian subcontinent.

stem: The prehistoric paintings were usually made at places that were __________.
solution: The shelters chosen were generally accessible and located near water sources.

stem: Which period's paintings are the oldest at Bhimbetka?
solution: The Upper Palaeolithic paintings are the oldest at Bhimbetka.

stem: The green and yellow tinges in some animal figures were used to depict __________.
options: animals like rhinos and cattle in swaying movement
solution: Green and dark red were often used to depict swaying animals such as rhinos and cattle.

stem: The rock painting sites indicate that prehistoric humans had a well-developed sense of __________.
solution: The detailed paintings show a keen sense of observation and artistic expression.

stem: The tradition of rock painting in India continued into the __________ period at some sites.
solution: At some sites, the rock painting tradition continued into the historic period.

stem: The human figures in Mesolithic paintings are often shown __________.
options: in dynamic activity such as hunting and dancing
solution: Mesolithic humans are shown in lively activities like hunting, dancing and food gathering.

stem: The prehistoric artist obtained black colour from __________.
solution: Black was obtained from charcoal or manganese.

stem: The concentration of hand prints and finger markings in some shelters may represent __________.
solution: Hand prints and finger markings are interpreted as early symbolic or ritual expression.

stem: The subjects of prehistoric paintings rarely include __________.
solution: Temples and written texts do not appear; the art predates them, focusing on animals and daily life.

stem: The rock shelters of Bhimbetka lie within a __________ forest region.
solution: Bhimbetka lies amid dense deciduous forest in the Vindhya hills.

stem: Prehistoric paintings are a valuable source for reconstructing the __________ of ancient India.
solution: They help reconstruct the cultural life and environment of prehistoric India.

stem: The number of rock shelters identified at Bhimbetka runs into __________.
solution: Bhimbetka has several hundred rock shelters, many with paintings.

stem: The images of animals like the elephant and bison at Bhimbetka are usually painted in __________.
solution: Large animals are typically rendered in red and white.

stem: The theme of a wounded animal or a hunting accident in the paintings reflects the __________ of early life.
solution: Such scenes reflect the dangers faced during hunting in prehistoric life.

stem: The oldest paintings are found on the __________ of the rock shelters, less exposed to weather.
solution: The older, better-preserved paintings survive on protected inner walls and ceilings.

stem: Prehistoric rock art demonstrates that art is a __________ human activity.
solution: Rock art shows that artistic expression is very ancient and found across human cultures.

stem: The prehistoric painters often depicted animals __________ human figures in size, emphasising their importance.
solution: Animals were frequently drawn larger than humans, showing their central role in early life.

stem: The rock shelters were used by prehistoric humans mainly as __________.
solution: The shelters served as dwellings for prehistoric humans.

stem: The continuity of the rock painting tradition over thousands of years shows its role in __________.
solution: The long tradition reflects the transmission of culture across generations.

stem: Which Indian state, besides Madhya Pradesh, is well known for prehistoric rock art at sites like Lakhudiyar?
solution: Uttarakhand (Lakhudiyar) is another important prehistoric rock art region.

stem: The importance of Bhimbetka lies in its __________ record of continuous human occupation and art.
solution: Bhimbetka preserves a long, continuous record of human occupation and artistic activity.

stem: Prehistoric rock paintings are considered '__________ art' because they were made before the invention of writing.
solution: They are called prehistoric because they predate written records.

stem: The prehistoric rock paintings were discovered at Bhimbetka in the year __________.
solution: V. S. Wakankar discovered the Bhimbetka paintings in 1957–58.

stem: The prehistoric period during which humans first used tools of chipped stone and made the earliest paintings is the __________.
solution: The Palaeolithic (Old Stone Age) is when the earliest rock paintings appear.

stem: The subjects of Mesolithic rock paintings show that people lived mainly by __________.
solution: The hunting scenes reflect a hunting-and-gathering way of life in the Mesolithic.

stem: The animals in prehistoric paintings are shown __________ in relation to the tiny human figures.
solution: Animals are shown large and dominant compared with the small human hunters.

stem: The bright colour absent from the prehistoric palette, due to lack of natural sources, was __________.
solution: Blue was largely absent; the palette was red, white, green, yellow and black.

stem: The green pigment in prehistoric painting was derived from a green variety of __________.
solution: Green came from a green variety of chalcedony (a quartz mineral).

stem: The prehistoric artist most likely used __________ to apply paint to the rock.
options: fingers and simple brushes of fibre/hair
solution: Prehistoric artists used fingers and simple brushes of plant fibre or animal hair.

stem: The rock paintings depict community activities such as __________.
solution: The paintings show dancing, group hunting and community rituals.

stem: The prehistoric paintings help us understand the __________ of early humans, since they left no writing.
solution: The paintings are a key source for the way of life and environment of pre-literate humans.

stem: The prehistoric rock shelters continued to be painted into the __________ period at some sites.
solution: At some sites the tradition of painting continued into the early historic period.

stem: The superimposition of layers of paintings at Bhimbetka indicates that the shelters were used __________.
options: over a very long span of time
solution: Layered, overlapping paintings show use over a very long span of time.

stem: The prehistoric paintings of Kupgallu, Piklihal and Tekkalkota are located in __________ India.
solution: These rock-painting sites are in South India.

stem: The colours have survived for thousands of years because they were made from __________ that bond with the rock.
solution: Durable mineral oxides (like haematite) bonded with the rock and survived for millennia.

stem: The prehistoric artists chose to paint deep inside shelters partly to __________.
solution: Painting on protected inner surfaces helped shield the images from weathering.

stem: The recurring depiction of the horse and rider appears mainly in the __________ paintings.
solution: Horses and riders appear in the later (Chalcolithic and historic) phase paintings.

stem: The subject matter of the earliest (Upper Palaeolithic) paintings is dominated by __________.
solution: The earliest paintings are dominated by large wild animals.

stem: Prehistoric rock art is significant as the __________ evidence of artistic activity in India.
solution: Rock art is the earliest evidence of artistic activity in India.

stem: The rock shelters at Bhimbetka were also used by prehistoric people as __________.
solution: The shelters served as dwellings for prehistoric people.
